A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable manuscripts and appendices describing the same DCPO study. Equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched across the reorganization; internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SD 2.1 fine-tuning experiments, caption statistics, perturbation and distribution-shift analyses, and GPT-4o evaluations in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Rapidata and SDXL experiments, online and iterative comparisons, perturbation-judge analyses, and a human evaluation.

M1.justification: The DCPO training loss and captioning, perturbation, and hybrid variants are retained. v2 expands the description of CLIPScore-based perturbation selection, presenting it as the original procedure, and tests alternative judges as ablations. This does not establish a change to the underlying DCPO algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds training on Rapidata alongside the retained Pick-a-Pic v2/Pick-Double Caption data. The text-to-image task and existing evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. SDXL is an additional model configuration, not additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SPO and SePPO comparisons in Table 6 and four alternative perturbation judges in Figure 8. It also adds Diffusion-DPO to the beta-sensitivity comparison, previously limited to DCPO-h. Existing baselines, including the appendix Diffusion-KTO comparison, are retained.

E3.justification: v1 reports using published baseline hyperparameters; v2 reports method-specific searches and expands the beta sweep with a 2000 setting. Added experiments introduce SDXL LoRA fine-tuning, VQAScore analysis, fixed-budget online comparisons, a 100-pair study with three human raters, and GPT-4o image-position controls.

E4.justification: v2 adds VQAScore verification of semantic overlap, comparisons of alternative perturbation-selection judges, an expanded comparative beta analysis, and human and positional-bias checks on GPT-4o evaluation. The original perturbation-strength, caption-quality, and distribution-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The same-seed comparison statement and Figure 5 regression display are retained. v2 supplies no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its per-volunteer percentages and average are additional point estimates rather than a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace MaPO's PickScore 19.41, HPSv2.1 24.47, and GenEval 0.4106 with 20.31, 25.31, and 0.4938 under the revised tuning account; the main DCPO scores remain unchanged. Substantial new results cover Rapidata, SDXL, SPO/SePPO, perturbation judges, beta settings, VQAScore, and evaluator validation.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 6 corrects the losing-trajectory conditioning written in v1 Equation 1. It also omits the standalone Gaussian reverse-transition and denoising-objective formulas from v1 Appendix A.1. The hypotheses and DCPO proofs remain essentially unchanged; preference-optimization mathematics moves into Section 2.

C1.justification: The dual-caption contribution and broad performance claims remain. However, the introduction narrows the stated advantage over existing methods from +0.45 to +0.31 on HPSv2.1 and from +3% to +2% on GenEval, following the revised baseline results.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning fixed-budget efficiency, CLIPScore selection versus MLLM judges, and human–GPT-4o agreement. The unexplored-SDXL limitation becomes a qualification about preliminary evidence, and preprocessing costs are described as one-time expenses. Its revised claim that beta 5000 performs best across metrics conflicts with Table 12.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with batch sizes, learning-rate and beta grids, selected configurations, and a newly stated 2000-step training budget. It documents SDXL LoRA use, perturbation-selection details, judge rubrics, and captioning time. The existing GPU configuration and code/data link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to semantic similarity in preference-data selection, online and iterative optimization, and MLLM judging, with citations supporting the new datasets and backbone experiments. Several earlier general alignment references are removed. The central positioning as an extension of Diffusion-DPO remains.

P1.justification: Much of the original exposition and proof prose is retained. Edits replace 'conflict distribution' with 'semantic overlap', revise the abstract and related-work discussion, move preference background into a preliminary section, and reorganize the training appendix into method-specific explanations.

P2.justification: The journal format changes typography, author layout, table styling, and figure sizing and placement. New comparison tables and judge/VQAScore plots are added, and the beta table expands. Appendix galleries enlarge and reuse examples already present in Figure 1. The standalone beta plot disappears, but its underlying results remain.

improvement.justification: The added dataset/backbone tests, evaluator checks, and explicit baseline searches address v1's limited generalization evidence and sparse tuning documentation. However, mismatched metric labels in Figure 8, inconsistent human percentages in Table 14, and the beta-optimality claim contradicted by Table 12 weaken the additions. The net improvement is useful but limited.
